data.name: InAllowedYouCanEnableAllowedWebsites
data.value: In Allowed, you can enable Allowed websites only for Chrome and Edge: it blocks other websites and replaces the blocked website list during a session or schedule. When adding a domain, select Include all subdomains or enter *.example.com to allow its subdomains at any depth. Without that option, the domain and its www variant are allowed. It does not include other domains the site uses for images or files; add those separately. After changes, copy chrome://policy or edge://policy from Allowed and paste the address into the corresponding browser. Press Enter, then click Reload policies and reload the affected tab. Normal policy reloads do not require closing the browser. Check URLBlocklist and URLAllowlist: writing rules does not verify that the browser has read them. Other browsers, applications and Edge profiles with personal Microsoft accounts are not covered. Existing policies from other tools are not overwritten. Internal browser pages and developer tools remain available.

data.value: How to identify failing images and files

data.name: ResourceInstructions
data.value:
On the affected site, open F12 → Network, reload the page and reproduce the failure. Copy failing request URLs (one per line), or export HAR (sanitized) and import it here. If F12 is still blocked, inspect browser policies.
Analysis is local and makes no network requests. Only domains and error categories are kept in memory; HAR files, headers and paths are not stored. Candidates have status 0, a network error or HTTP 4xx/5xx. Failures may also involve authentication, CORS, cancellation or the server. blob:, data:, IPs and other schemes are skipped. Select only domains you recognize; none are added automatically.
